odia: ବାପ ଦେହେରି, ପୁଅ ପୁଜାରି, ଗଣ୍ଡି ମଣ୍ଡ ସବୁ ତୁମ୍ଭରି
title: Every role in the same hands
literal_meaning: Father is the deity’s servant, son the priest; body and head are all yours.
explanation: The father-and-son pairing gathers the roles into one circle. The dictionary explicitly explains the saying as “you have become all-in-all here.” Our reading follows the teasing accusation of concentrated control: who is left to question a decision? The image does not establish wrongdoing by a family or religious occupation. Its application to a modern committee is our own.
meaning_odia: ବାପ ଓ ପୁଅଙ୍କ ଭୂମିକାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି ସବୁକିଛି ଗୋଟିଏ ପରିସରରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେ—ତୁମ୍ଭେ ଏଠାରେ ସର୍ବେସର୍ବା ହୋଇଛ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କ୍ଷମତା ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଯିବାର ଟାହି ଅଛି: ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିକୁ ପଚାରିବାକୁ ଆଉ କିଏ ରହିଲା? ଏହା କୌଣସି ପରିବାର ବା ଧାର୍ମିକ ବୃତ୍ତିର ଦୋଷର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଆଜିର ସମିତି ସହ ତୁଳନା ଆମର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ।
english_summary: The source’s all-in-all gloss gives a teasing picture of concentrated authority.
odia_summary: ସର୍ବେସର୍ବା ହୋଇ ବସିବାର ଟାହି ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଆସେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: At a club meeting, the same two people write the rules, approve the spending and decide every complaint. A member quotes the father-and-son line and asks for another person to review decisions. No actual religious institution or family is being described.
cultural_context: The headword is marked Sambalpur regional usage, not an exclusive origin. Religious roles supply the image; no present community practice or universal family trait is inferred.
